- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) and forecast is trending up, reduce upward bias — model tends to overreact.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.3) and forecast is trending down, reduce downward bias — model tends to overcorrect.
- If recent price history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days of decline followed by rebound), model often overshoots the true mean — dampen forecast peaks.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overestimates continuation — cap forecast growth to 2–3% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.3–0.6) and forecast is volatile, favor smoother, trend-following adjustments — avoid overfitting to short-term noise.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent momentum — not just historical mean.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” signals (e.g., +0.3 → -0.3 → +0.3), model often misreads direction — align forecast with sentiment swing midpoint, not peak.
